- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- In high-sentiment environments, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; adjust downward by 5–10% for 30-day horizons.  
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce next period’s forecast by 5–8% to prevent momentum overhang.  
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.6), model often misreads trend — use 3-period moving average of true values as a sanity check before finalizing forecast.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days), model tends to lag — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to compensate for lag.
